an9.42:1.1: On one occasion Ven. Ānanda was staying near Kosambī at Ghosita’s monastery.
an9.42:1.2: Then Ven. Udāyin went to him and, on arrival, exchanged courteous greetings.
an9.42:1.3: After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he sat to one side. As he was sitting there, he said to Ven. Ānanda,
an9.42:1.4: “This has been said by Pañcālacaṇḍa the deva’s son:
an9.42:2.1: ‘Truly in a confining place, he found an opening—
an9.42:2.3: the awakened one who awakened through jhāna,
an9.42:2.4: the chief bull, withdrawn, the sage.’
an9.42:3.1: “Now which, my friend, is the confining place? And which opening in the confining place is the Blessed One said to have attained?”
an9.42:3.2: [Ven. Ānanda:] “The five strings of sensuality, my friend, are described by the Blessed One as a confining place.
an9.42:3.4: Forms cognizable via the eye—agreeable, pleasing, charming, endearing, enticing, linked to sensual desire;
an9.42:3.8: tactile sensations cognizable via the body—agreeable, pleasing, charming, endearing, enticing, linked to sensual desire.
an9.42:3.9: These five strings of sensuality are described by the Blessed One as a confining place.
an9.42:4.1: “Now there is the case where a monk—quite secluded from sensuality, secluded from unskillful qualities—enters & remains in the first jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.
an9.42:4.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:4.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:4.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:4.5: Just that directed thought & evaluation have not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:5.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the stilling of directed thoughts & evaluations, enters & remains in the second jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of concentration, unification of awareness free from directed thought & evaluation—internal assurance.
an9.42:5.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:5.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:5.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:5.5: Just that rapture has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:6.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the fading of rapture, remains in equanimity, mindful & alert, senses pleasure with the body, and enters & remains in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous & mindful, he has a pleasant abiding.’
an9.42:6.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:6.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:6.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:6.5: Just that the pleasure of equanimity has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:7.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the abandoning of pleasure & pain—as with the earlier disappearance of elation & distress—enters & remains in the fourth jhāna: purity of equanimity & mindfulness, neither pleasure nor pain.
an9.42:7.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:7.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:7.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:7.5: Just that the perception of form has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:8.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the complete transcending of perceptions of (physical) form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and not attending to perceptions of multiplicity, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite space,’ enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of space.
an9.42:8.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:8.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:8.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:8.5: Just that the perception of the dimension of the infinitude of space has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:9.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the complete transcending of the dimension of the infinitude of space, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite consciousness,’ enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness.
an9.42:9.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:9.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:9.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:9.5: Just that the perception of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:10.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the complete transcending of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, (perceiving,) ‘There is nothing,’ enters & remains in the dimension of nothingness.
an9.42:10.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:10.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:10.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:10.5: Just that the perception of the dimension of nothingness has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:11.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the complete transcending of the dimension of nothingness, enters & remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.
an9.42:11.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, though followed by a sequel.
an9.42:11.3: For even there, there’s a confining place.
an9.42:11.4: What is the confining place there?
an9.42:11.5: Just that the perception of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception has not ceased. This is the confining place there.
an9.42:12.1: “Then there is the case where a monk, with the complete transcending of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters & remains in the cessation of perception & feeling. And as he sees (that) with discernment, effluents are completely ended.
an9.42:12.2: Even this much is described by the Blessed One as the attaining of an opening in a confining place, without a sequel.”
